conventions.convention: Spaces and continuous duals are real. The dual pairing is evaluation. Subgradients satisfy R(z) ≥ R(x) + ⟨ξ,z−x⟩ for every z; their existence is assumed where needed, not guaranteed by properness and convexity. In convex combinations, 0·(+∞)=0.
D_R^ξ†(x,x†)=R(x)−R(x†)−⟨ξ†,x−x†⟩. The first argument is the comparison point; the second carries the selected subgradient.

The VSC holds on the named regularizer sublevel, uses the p-th power of the exact-data residual, and requires 0 ≤ β < 1. Its index is continuous, nondecreasing, concave, zero at zero, and positive elsewhere.
Extend −ψ by +∞ on negative arguments and use H(q)=sup_{s≥0}(ψ(s)−qs), for positive q. The conjugate bounds require positive c₁,c₂,C₃,α and finiteness at both displayed arguments.

The objective is p⁻¹ times the p-th power of the residual plus αR. Approximate minimizers are global up to εδ=O(δᵖ). With c_p=2^(1−p)/p and ρδ=H(c_p/α), parameter coupling requires αρδ comparable to δᵖ and a bounded ratio H(c_p/(2α))/ρδ. Minimizer existence is conditional.
The logarithmic index is capped at t₀ with 0<t₀<exp(−(ν+1)); the parameter is α(δ)=δᵖ(log(1/δ))^ν for sufficiently small positive δ.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated continuous nondecreasing concave ψ with ψ(0)=0 and H(q)=sup_{s≥0}(ψ(s)−qs), assuming the displayed conjugate values are finite: if c₁r+c₂αe ≤ d+αψ(C₃r), with c₁,c₂,C₃,α>0 and d,r,e≥0, then e ≤ c₂⁻¹(d/α+H(c₁/(C₃α))) and r ≤ (2/c₁)(d+αH(c₁/(2C₃α))).

Under the stated real-Banach VSC on L_R₀ with R₀>R(x†), selected subgradient, 1≤p<∞, β<1, conjugate assumptions, supplied global εδ-minimizers with εδ=O(δᵖ), α→0, αρδ comparable to δᵖ, and H(c_p/(2α))≤C_Hρδ, the minimizers eventually belong to L_R₀, their Bregman errors are O(ρδ), and their noisy-data residuals are O(δ). The additional stated index bound gives absolute penalty error O(ρδ); a Bregman lower bound c_R‖x−x†‖ˢ gives norm error to power s of order O(ρδ). The stated quadratic Hilbert specialization with α comparable to δ gives solution error O(√δ) and residual O(δ), conditional on supplied exact global minimizers.
For a proper convex R on a real Banach space, x†∈dom R and ξ†∈∂R(x†), define D_R^ξ†(x,x†)=R(x)−R(x†)−⟨ξ†,x−x†⟩ for x∈dom R. This is nonnegative and vanishes at x=x†.

With the stated real Banach spaces, forward map, exact solution, proper convex regularizer, selected subgradient, exponent 1≤p<∞, index ψ, coefficient 0≤β<1 and level R₀≥R(x†), the VSC is −⟨ξ†,x−x†⟩ ≤ βD_R^ξ†(x,x†)+ψ(‖F(x)−F(x†)‖ᵖ) for every x∈D(F) with R(x)≤R₀.
For proper convex R on a real Banach space, x∈dom R and ξ∈X*, R(x)+R*(ξ)≥⟨ξ,x⟩, with equality if and only if ξ∈∂R(x).

seams_checked.note: The rate theorem's Hilbert clause preserves the open real-Hilbert forward-map domain and the global exact-solution meaning of x₀-minimum norm. Its generic Banach clause does not import differentiability or a tangential-cone hypothesis.

The quadratic Hilbert objective matches def-ip-nonlinear-tikhonov-functional, including both factors of 1/2. The rate theorem explicitly assumes supplied global minimizers and does not claim existence from the functional's definition.

This is a page prerequisite only: the Landweber algorithm and theorem make no item-level citation to the assigned VSC results. They explicitly claim neither a convergence rate nor minimum-norm selection, so they do not overstate the VSC theorem.

The joint and frozen estimates preserve the subgradient sign, Bregman orientation, and sublevel restriction. The joint theorem applies the conjugate lemma with c₁=1, c₂=1−b and C₃=C_*; the frozen lemma uses c₁=c₂=1 and C₃ equal to its displayed positive constant. Both conjugate arguments and residual factors agree with the supplier.

The certificate definition uses the same real-dual subgradient and Bregman orientation. The attainment lemma preserves both directions of Fenchel–Young equality, derives a β=0 VSC with ψ(s)=(1+‖p†‖)√s, verifies its conjugate coupling for α comparable to δ, and applies the rate theorem only to supplied global minimizers.
